newsitem.title: USA: House panel approves wildlife law exemptions.
newsitem.headline: House panel approves wildlife law exemptions.

text.p: A House panel Wednesday passed a bill to exempt most flood control activities, such as repairing and maintaining levees, from federal requirements to protect endangered wildlife.
Backers of the bill, which passed the House Resources Committee 22-9, said it was needed to allow speedy repairs and maintenance of flood control facilities.

But opponents said the bill was just a way to weaken the Endangered Species Act, and said it was written broadly enough to exempt many hydroelectric dams from various requirements to protect endangered salmon and other fish.

Rep. Richard Pombo, a California Republican who sponsored the bill, has argued that flood damage this winter in his central California district worsened because maintenance of levees was stalled by efforts to protect the endangered elderberry beetle, which lived in bushes near the levee.

But the Clinton administration, which opposed Pombo's bill, said beetle protections had no effect on the floods and said the bill would give flood districts overly broad exemptions from the wildlife protection law.

"This administration has consistently opposed waivers of environmental laws and will continue to do so. Such waivers can cause serious environmental problems and set a dangerous precedent by encouraging other similar waivers," Interior Deputy Secretay John Garamendi said in a letter to the committee.
